'''PHP2Shell''' is a pair of high-impact [[Vulnerability (computer security)|computer vulnerabilities]] ('''CVE-2026-109618'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-109618|title=CVE-2026-109618|publisher=Mitre}}</ref> and '''CVE-2026-109619'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-109619|title=CVE-2026-109619|publisher=Mitre}}</ref>) in [[PHP]] versions 5.4{{endash}}8.5 that allow [[Arbitrary code execution|remote code execution]] (RCE), potentially allowing a malicious user to gain remote control of the website host. PHP is a popular programming language that many website architectures are built upon, with the two vulnerabilities estimated to affect nearly 70% of the commercial [[world wide web]].

Their existence was publicly announced on 20 October 2026.<ref name="oct20">{{Cite web |date=20 October 2026 |title=PHP: News Archive - 20 Oct 2026 |url=https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-20-1 |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=www.php.net |language=en}}</ref> An emergency [[Patch (computing)|patch]] for versions 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 and details about the vulnerabilities were released the following day, with numerous websites temporarily taken offline to apply the patches before exploits could be used.<ref name="oct21">{{Cite web |date=21 October 2026 |title=PHP: News Archive - 21 Oct 2026 |url=https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5|access-date=21 October 2026 |website=www.php.net |language=en}}</ref>

==Discovery==
The vulnerabilities were independently discovered by two parties: Ryan Austin, a researcher at the [[California]]-based security firm Calif,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Volz |first1=Dustin |title=A Hacking Tool Built With A.I. Can Breach Phones Without a Click |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/08/us/politics/calif-ai-worm-wechat-hack.html |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=The New York Times |date=8 September 2026}}</ref> as part of the [[OpenAI]] "Patch the Planet" project in August 2026, and the Israeli–American cloud security company [[Wiz, Inc.|Wiz]], a subsidiary of [[Alphabet Inc.]] and a part of [[Google Cloud]].<ref name="McMillan2026" details="{{subref|q=Ryan Austin, a researcher at Calif, uncovered the flaws with help from GPT-5.6 Sol, one of OpenAI's most advanced models, during an audit of PHP's source code in August. ... Researchers from Google's Wiz cybersecurity team soon reached out with new exploits, which they had discovered independent of Calif. }}" /> Austin used OpenAI's [[GPT-5.6 Sol]] model to assist with finding the vulnerability.<ref name="McMillan2026" details="{{subref|q=Ryan Austin, a researcher at Calif, uncovered the flaws with help from GPT-5.6 Sol, one of OpenAI's most advanced models, during an audit of PHP's source code in August. ... Researchers from Google's Wiz cybersecurity team soon reached out with new exploits, which they had discovered independent of Calif. }}" /> Wiz researchers used the large language models [[Gemini (language model)|Gemini 4 Argon]] and GPT-5.6 Sol, as well as their own tool, Wiz Atlas, to help with their research.<ref  name="Satter2026" />

PHP versions as early as 5.4 (released in 2012)<ref>{{Cite web |title=PHP: Releases |url=https://www.php.net/releases/index.php |access-date=22 October 2026 |website=www.php.net |language=en}}</ref> were affected by these vulnerabilities, and while concerns around [[memory safety]] bugs had been raised decades before, no action was taken at the time because it was not thought that developing a working [[Exploit (computer security)|exploit]] could be feasible.<ref name="Kan2026" /><ref name="McMillan2026" details="{{subref|q=The class of bugs had been hiding in PHP's source code for years. A security researcher had flagged it as a problem area decades earlier, but the flaw had been considered too difficult to exploit and was largely forgotten, Duong said.}}">{{cite news |last1=McMillan |first1=Robert |title=Exclusive {{!}} AI Just Found a Bug That Puts up to 70% of the World's Websites at Risk |url=https://www.wsj.com/tech/cybersecurity/ai-just-found-a-bug-that-puts-up-to-70-of-the-worlds-websites-at-risk-fd0902ea |url-access=subscription |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=Wall Street Journal |date=21 October 2026}}</ref> A PHP core developer discovered the [[Out of memory|out-of-memory]] error behind one of the vulnerabilities during an audit in 2024, but the [[Software bug|bug]] was never fixed; the development team could not reach consensus on how to do so and a specific exploit had not yet been discovered, so the issue was not prioritized.<ref name="Constantin2026">{{cite news |last1=Constantin |first1=Ana Maria |title=PHP knew about one of the flaws in 2024 but could not agree a fix |url=https://thenextweb.com/news/php-foundation-structural-failure-2024-flaw-leak |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=The Next Web |date=21 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security |url=https://thephp.foundation/blog/2026/10/21/todays-php-security-release-and-how-were-strengthening-php-security/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=thephp.foundation |language=en}}</ref>

The vulnerability was rated 9.2 (critical) out of 10 under [[Common Vulnerability Scoring System|CVSS]] v4.0 by PHP developers,<ref>{{Cite web |title=php.announce: [ANNOUNCE] Upcoming Critical PHP Security Release |url=https://news-web.php.net/php.announce/509 |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=news-web.php.net}}</ref> while security firm watchTowr rated it a full 10.0.<ref name="Abrams">{{Cite web |last=Abrams |first=Lawrence |title=PHP warns admins of two critical flaws, emergency patches coming tomorrow |url=https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/php-warns-admins-of-two-critical-flaws-emergency-patches-coming-tomorrow/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=BleepingComputer |language=en-us}}</ref>

==Patches==
The maintainers of PHP released patched versions of PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5 (8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12).<ref name="oct21" /> [[Source code]] patches were released for version 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, but no official updated [[Binary file|binaries]] for those versions were released as they are considered [[Software release life cycle#End-of-life|end of life]].<ref name="oct21" /> Temporary mitigations were also published, but the maintainers said there were no complete mitigations and that updating was the only safe choice.<ref name="oct21" /> Both vulnerabilities were published through [[GitHub]] security advisories on 21 October 2026 at 13:34 UTC,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w|title=RCE via OOM corruption|date=21 October 2026|access-date=21 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp|title=RCE via stale global state|date=21 October 2026|access-date=21 October 2026}}</ref> 26 minutes before the announced release time, with the PHP website updated shortly thereafter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scherzer |first=Daniel |date=22 October 2026 |title=Blog: PHP2Shell: a Timeline |url=https://scherzer.dev/Blog/20261022-php2shell-timeline |access-date=22 October 2026 |website=scherzer.dev |language=en}}</ref>

The PHP maintainers announced the update early and before release, after news of the vulnerabilities leaked on 20 October on the [[Hacker News]] forums,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tell HN: 2x PHP RCE CVEs with CVSS 10.0 Incoming |url=https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50167754 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261021192245/https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50167754 |archive-date=21 October 2026 |access-date=22 October 2026 |website=news.ycombinator.com |language=en}}</ref> in a post on [[X (social network)|X]] by cybersecurity company watchTowr labs, and in a [[proof-of-concept]] exploit video mistakenly released by Calif.<ref name="McMillan2026" details="{{subref|q=News of the patch leaked out Tuesday, in a post to Hacker News, just under two days before the patch release.}}" /><ref name="Constantin2026" /> The early notice on PHP.net encouraged users to prepare and update as soon as the patch was released.<ref name="oct21" /> One security firm, Sansec, expected "mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodin |first=Dan |date=20 October 2026 |title=PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently |url=https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10/php-maintainers-tell-web-devs-to-prepare-themselves-for-critical-security-patches/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=Ars Technica |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261021121524/https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10/php-maintainers-tell-web-devs-to-prepare-themselves-for-critical-security-patches/|archive-date=21 October 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Proof-of-concept exploits, write-ups, and partial mitigations started circulating on the [[Internet]] before the end of the embargo, after development platform Chainguard released patched versions of the software early; this allowed attackers to determine what code had been changed.<ref name="Abrams" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Only for the curious... |url=https://jackalsyn.com/posts/php-up-2026.html |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=jackalsyn.com}}</ref><ref name="Constantin2026" />

[[Amazon Web Services|Amazon]] Threat Intelligence identified a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt dating back to 17 October 2026, in MadPot telemetry, four days before public disclosure.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 October 2026 |title=Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot {{!}} AWS Security Blog |url=https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/amazon-threat-intelligence-identifies-php2shell-exploitation-prior-to-public-disclosure-in-madpot/ |access-date=22 October 2026 |website=aws.amazon.com}}</ref> [[Cloudflare]] reported signs of early exploitation prior to public [[Patch (computing)|patch]] release, and deployed temporary [[web application firewall]] rules as an attempted stopgap mitigation against the vulnerability.<ref name="Gatlan2026">{{Cite web |last=Gatlan |first=Sergiu |date=21 October 2026 |title=PHP ships emergency patches for critical PHP2Shell flaws |url=https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/php-ships-emergency-patches-for-critical-php2shell-flaws/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=BleepingComputer |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=21 October 2026 |title=Hold on to your butts: Web admins braced for emergency PHP updates to plug leaked exploits |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/software/security/we-expect-mass-attacks-to-start-within-15-minutes-of-the-release-web-admins-braced-for-emergency-php-updates-to-plug-leaked-high-severity-holes/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Knecht |first1=Dane |title=Dane Knecht 🦭 (@dok2001) on X |url=https://x.com/dok2001/status/2112811965735202970 |website=X (formerly Twitter) |date=21 October 2026}}</ref> Security firm watchTowr said it had observed exploitation in the wild by 21 October through its [[Honeypot (computing)|honeypot]] network,<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 October 2026 |title=PHP RCE FAQ: PHP2Shell CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619 |url=https://watchtowr.com/intelligence/php-cve-2026-109618-faq/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=watchTowr |language=en}}</ref> while the [[US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency]] said it had not observed exploitation as of the same day.<ref name="Collier2026" />

== Impact ==
[[File:Php2shell wiki.png|thumb|Warning posted on the [[English Wikipedia]] about community-owned tools being offline due to the PHP2Shell incident.]]
The potential impacts of the vulnerability were widespread. Approximately 69% of websites whose server-side programming language is known by [[W3Techs]] use PHP, including those that use [[content management system]]s such as [[Drupal]], [[Joomla]], and [[WordPress]].<ref name="Collier2026" details="Citing {{Cite web |title=Usage statistics of PHP for websites |url=https://w3techs.com/technologies/details/pl-php |access-date=2026-10-23 |website=W3Techs}}">{{cite news |last1=Collier |first1=Kevin |title=Critical vulnerabilities in commonly used web code spark rush to update systems |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/security/critical-vulnerabilities-php-update-systems-rcna604751 |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=NBC News |date=21 October 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="bbc">{{cite news |last1=Gerkin |first1=Tom |title=Websites taken down worldwide as critical PHP cyber-security update issued |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmly0lg3w5x2o |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=BBC News |date=21 October 2026}}</ref> PHP is also bundled with vendor appliances, [[web hosting service|web host]] control panels such as [[cPanel]] and [[Plesk]], and some [[Windows (Operating system)|Windows]] applications.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hammond |first=John |date=21 October 2026 |title=Rapid Response: php2shell, Leaked Critical PHP Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619) |url=https://www.huntress.com/blog/php2shell-leaked-critical-php-vulnerabilities |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=Huntress |language=en}}</ref>

Following advice from [[Computer emergency response team|CERT]]-EU and the [[National Cyber Security Centre (United Kingdom)|British National Cyber Security Centre]] (NCSC), many organizations across Europe took their websites offline as a precaution while the patches were pending, including the Dutch government portal Overheid.nl, the Danish national school communication platform, all Finnish government public-facing web services, and all websites of the [[Ministry of the Interior (France)|French Interior Ministry]].<ref name="Satter2026">{{Cite news |last=Satter |first=Raphael |last2=Marchandon |first2=Leo |last3=Ghosh |first3=Kanjyik |last4=Pardesi |first4=Rajveer |date=21 October 2026 |title=Government websites go dark after AI-discovered flaw sparks security scramble |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/eu-agency-warns-websites-may-need-be-taken-offline-php-prepares-patches-2026-10-21/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref The [[Wikimedia Foundation]] shut down many of their supporting services, and [[Internet forum|forum]] sites such as [[4chan]] and [[Something Awful]] went offline.<ref name="Collier2026" /><ref name="Tauber-2026">{{Cite web |last=Tauber |first=Olivia |date=21 October 2026 |title=PHP vulnerability: Which websites and services are affected? |url=https://mashable.com/tech/php-vulnerability-websites-offline-affected-services |access-date=21 October 2026 |website=Mashable |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Kan2026" /> Several Japanese websites and applications also went offline, including games such as ''[[Umamusume: Pretty Derby]]'', ''[[Granblue Fantasy]]'', ''[[Princess Connect! Re:Dive]]'', and numerous [[e-commerce]] sites.<ref name="ITmedia-21oct2026">{{cite news|url=https://www.itmedia.co.jp/news/article/2610/21/2000002472/|date=21 October 2026|title=著名ITサービス相次いで緊急メンテへ　コドモン、シャドバ、BASE、さくらのレンタルサーバなど　「PHP」脆弱性に起因か|trans-title=Several prominent IT services—including Codmon, Shadowverse, BASE, and Sakura Rental Server—have initiated emergency maintenance, likely due to a vulnerability in PHP|publisher=ITmedia|access-date=21 October 2026 |language=ja}}</ref><ref name="Tauber-2026" /> The [[Internet Archive]] briefly shut down to fix the issue.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Paul |last2=Mizen |first2=Ronald |date=21 October 2026 |title=AI just discovered a bug putting 70pc of world's websites at risk |url=https://www.afr.com/world/north-america/websites-go-dark-as-ai-discovered-bug-sparks-global-security-scramble-20261022-p617nf |access-date=22 October 2026 |website=Australian Financial Review |language=en}}</ref>


== Analysis ==
Researchers at Wiz stated that the issue was on par with [[Heartbleed]], a 2014 vulnerability that affected OpenSSL, an encryption library used by about two-thirds of the web at the time.<ref>{{cite news |last=Eadicicco |first=Lisa |title=Global websites shut down after AI found a critical flaw affecting 70% of the internet {{!}} CNN Business |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/10/21/tech/php2shell-vulnerability-ai |access-date=22 October 2026 |work=CNN |date=21 October 2026}}</ref> Commentary in ''[[The Guardian]]'' noted that [[the PHP Foundation]], which maintains the PHP language, only had 13 full- and part-time employees, and relied on financial contributions, whereas AI research, which was credited with helping discover the vulnerability, received "billions" in investment.<ref>{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=Josh |title=What is PHP, and how bad is the computer language flaw causing website shutdowns globally? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/22/what-is-php-computer-language-flaw-causing-global-website-shutdowns |access-date=22 October 2026 |work=The Guardian |date=22 October 2026}}</ref> Coverage in ''[[The New York Times]]'' said that PHP was "pervasive" and speculated that "everyday users" could have their personal data put at risk.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Adam |first=Karla |last2=Volz |first2=Dustin |date=22 October 2026 |title=What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/22/technology/what-is-php-vulnerability-risks.html |access-date=22 October 2026 |work=The New York Times|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Czech volunteer Ondřej Surý was credited with playing a crucial role in automating the necessary patches.<ref>{{cite web |last=Warzel|first=Charlie|title='If Anything Happens to This Guy … Everyone Is Screwed'|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/2026/10/man-who-saved-internet-php-vulnerability/689123/?gift=nwn-guseqS6cY1kVeEKZAV4eM30ZQanhnWOnf22yy-c|work=The Atlantic|date=22 October 2026|access-date=23 October 2026}}</ref>
